assessment.scope: All worktree rows remain real DOM elements; no windowed rendering or deletion-policy changes.
assessment.profileScope: scan-settle profiles cover scan publications and waiting, not just the final scan-end interval. CPU profiles and browser counters overlap and must not be added together. Wall-time medians use separate runs without profiling.
rejectedCSS: content-visibility on table rows did not improve latency
content-visibility on text blocks did not meet targets
separate borders did not reduce paint cost
forced compositing did not reduce paint cost
content-visibility on cells reduced some layout work but worsened scrolling through intersection and layout work
assessment.remaining: Targets remain unmet. Sorting and full-review layout/style costs and scrolling paint dominate. Scan-end timing also includes the existing polling delay. Windowing would require redesigning logical navigation, active-descendant mounting, focus retention, accessible row exposure, and DOM-based test expectations before it is safe to consider.
